name: mr24

finding.region_hint: Changed return annotation at line 39 and element validation at lines 46-48
finding.title: Boolean task IDs bypass validation
finding.evidence: The function return annotation is list[int].
finding.explanation: Callers can receive a boolean value where the declared positive task-ID contract implies an integer identifier.
finding.suggested_follow_up: Reject bool explicitly before accepting integer task IDs.

reasoning_constraints: Boolean acceptance predates the diff; compare runtime behavior before and after.
Python bool is a subtype of int; list[int] alone does not exclude True.
Do not propose suppression of every annotation-only diff.

name: mr19
provenance: Pinned public source/diff and published/projected finding; callers supplied as reconstructed supplemental evidence, not captured model input.

finding.title: `completed` is no longer normalized to a boolean
finding.evidence: The original code returned `"completed": task["completed"] == True`.
finding.explanation: If task["completed"] can be a non-boolean truthy value, the API response can now expose a non-true/false value and change the response contract for callers.
finding.suggested_follow_up: Keep the field normalized to a boolean, or verify that upstream values are strictly boolean before passing them through.

reasoning_constraints: Supported HTTP writes validate completed as bool; storage creates False and batch completion assigns True.
Direct non-boolean helper calls genuinely change behavior, but are not proof of an HTTP regression.
A narrower local-contract concern is permitted by the current precision contract if its impact is supported.
